newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Senate drops electric deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Senate drops electric deregulation bill.

text.p: The Connecticut Senate has dropped a controversial proposal to restructure the state's electricity industry, state Sen. Melodie Peters (D) said on Wednesday.
Peters, co-chairwoman of the legislature's energy and technology committee, told Reuters she would work to reintroduce House bill 6774 in next year's legislative session which begins in February.
It was not immediately clear whether the House would pursue the bill during this legislative session, which ends on June 4.
"Yes, the bill is dead," Peters told Reuters.
"It's on hiatus. I am committed to working within the framework that we have established to move forward," she said. "I believe that competition is the right thing for this state."
"I believe that consumer choice is the right thing for this state. But how we get to that (rate) savings... the tradeoff for the consumer is not one I can live with."
While the House could still pursue the bill, it would need passage by both chambers and the governor's signature to become law.
